hints: Look closely at the boundary of the large central cell with the nucleus. Do you see only a thin plasma membrane, or a thick, dark, rigid outer cell wall as well?
Remember the three big plant-only features: a cellulose cell wall, a large permanent vacuole, and chloroplasts. Check the image for each one in turn.
walkthrough:
**Observe the cell boundary and interior**

Look at the edge of the main cell in the centre. It is bounded only by a thin cell surface membrane. There is no thick, rigid outer layer outside it.

Inside, you can see a nucleus with nucleolus, and many small oval organelles, but no huge fluid-filled sac taking up most of the cell.

**Recall animal versus plant differences**

Plant cells always have a cellulose cell wall outside the membrane, plus a large permanent vacuole and often chloroplasts.

Animal cells have only a plasma membrane as their outer boundary, no cell wall, no large permanent vacuole, and no chloroplasts.

**Match and conclude**

This cell has no cell wall, no large permanent vacuole, and no chloroplasts. The small oval structures are mitochondria, which both cell types have.

That combination fits an animal cell perfectly, so option A is the only valid conclusion.

options.A: Correct. The cell is bounded only by a plasma membrane with no rigid cell wall, which is characteristic of an animal cell.
options.B: Incorrect. A large permanent vacuole is a plant cell feature, not an animal feature, and no such vacuole is visible here.
options.C: Incorrect. The many small dark organelles are mitochondria, not chloroplasts, and there is no cell wall, so it is not a plant cell.
options.D: Incorrect. Lysosomes are mainly an animal cell feature, and the visible organelles are mitochondria, so this does not prove it is a plant cell.
